I’m afraid I don’t have live Internet access right now, so I can’t make a real-time call to a geocoding service for you.  
However, I can walk you through exactly how you’d obtain an address for a geographic point—once you supply **both** latitude *and* longitude—and give you a quick‑start snippet you can run yourself.

---

### What’s needed?

A reverse‑geocoding lookup requires:

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `lat`     | Latitude value (e.g., 74.98764). |
| `lng`/`lon` | Longitude value – without this the location can’t be pinpointed. |

If you only have one coordinate, you’ll first need to find its counterpart. Once you have both numbers, you can hit most public services.

---

### Example: Using the Google Maps Geocoding API  

```python
import requests

def google_reverse_geocode(lat, lng):
    api_key = "<YOUR_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY>"
    url = (
        f"https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?"
        f"latlng={lat},{lng}&key={api_key}"
    )
    resp = requests.get(url)
    data = resp.json()
    
    # Grab the formatted address from the first result
    if data["status"] == "OK":
        return data["results"][0]["formatted_address"]
    else:
        raise Exception(f"Geocoder error: {data['status']}")

address = google_reverse_geocode(74.98764, -122.12345)   # replace with your longitude
print(address)
```

> Replace `<YOUR_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY>` with a key you’ve generated in the Cloud Console.  
> Make sure billing is enabled; otherwise the free tier may not work.

---

### Other popular options

| Provider | Endpoint / Notes |
|----------|------------------|
| **OpenStreetMap Nominatim** | `https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?format=json&lat=<LAT>&lon=<LON>` |
| **HERE Geocoding & Search** | `https://rev-geocode.search.hereapi.com/v1/revgeo?q=<LAT>,<LON>&apikey=<APIKEY>` |
| **Bing Maps REST Services** | `http://dev.virtualearth.net/REST/v1/Locations/<LAT>,<LON>?ojson=true&mkt=en-US&key=<APIKEY>` |

All follow roughly the same pattern: send a GET request with the coordinates, receive a JSON payload containing the human‑readable address (`displayName`, `label`, etc.).

---

### Quick sanity check

Because you supplied only a latitude, double‑check whether you also have the matching longitude somewhere in your dataset. Without it, the API will either reject the request or return ambiguous results.

Once you add the longitude, just plug the two into one of the snippets above and you’re good to go!
